how: The initial proposal calls members to make a logo, while the later Tim proposal renews the call around another target.
A member proposes the logo and another joins, without evidence that the proposer placed pixels first.
Participants debate thickness, whitespace, and the red dot while also considering a mascot as a different target.
A red-dot completion report and a later report of the existing silver-bordered logo make progress visible in the thread.
Participants request, provide, and correct anchor coordinates while specifying pixel details.
Members ask for defense during expansion and ultimately prioritize retaining the small logo.
Distinguish distributing defense-script instructions from demonstrated execution or increased placements because the latter remain unobserved.
A direct assent answers the Tim call without asking anything back.
The proposed larger work encounters an active banner and a stated inability to find enough room.
A visitor reports resizing a neighboring mark to avoid overwriting the logo and apologizes for its apparent threat.
Participants discuss possible neighboring locations and a provisional agreement elsewhere without demonstrating a settled local border.
An incoming visitor offers reciprocal maintenance for building assistance, receives qualified willingness, and a later visitor receives thanks.
An incoming participant explicitly introduces themself as an ambassador while carrying a reciprocal-help proposal.
Members celebrate the completed logo with a declaration of success and praise.
Improvised coordinate selection demonstrates initiative but cannot establish whether the room decided who could direct others.
An aside about another unhappy college does not trace an actual changer or explain changed pixels.
In the blocked-expansion episode the speaker retains the existing small logo, so rebuilding after erasure is not needed to explain that choice.
A reciprocal-help proposal and friendly thanks do not establish a jointly adopted coalition.
A request to build below an existing logo does not establish ownership of that space or authority over guests.
The incoming proposal and its provisional hold contain no recorded dispute over who can bind a room.
The final coded contribution still directs active defense and cannot establish post-close disputes over preserved versions.
The mention of an unhappy college identifies neither a prior quarrel nor a named rival.
Logo and mascot proposals identify drawing subjects without establishing the candidate's broader ideological or historical conduct.
Anticipated conflict and an unnamed college do not show a prior tie naming a rival in an attack call.
The invitation and design proposals do not establish a host-subreddit prank or license to treat claims as false.
Difficulty noticing updates across comments does not establish a rule containing canvas discussion.
Design-reference images do not establish preservation of the final canvas or an account of the event.
Calling for a mascot during placement does not establish carrying the effort beyond the event.
In the blocked-expansion episode anticipated fighting is followed by an explicit choice to defend the existing logo rather than pursue that attack.
The passing remark about an unhappy college does not establish a continuing exchange of taunts or victory claims.
The invitation and completion reports do not establish which canvas placements the call caused.
The initial proposal is itself a call, leaving a distinct start-to-recruitment sequence unestablished.
Defense presupposes an existing logo, but edited passages cannot time a separate completion-to-maintenance transition.
Neighbor contact follows maintenance talk, but no passage attributes that contact to erosion of the maintained logo.
Reported preventive resizing does not establish a preceding settled border as the cause of restraint.
Retain the explicit defense-to-script recommendation while leaving the stronger manual-capacity-exhaustion mechanism unresolved.
Treat completion and celebration as co-present in the declaration of success rather than as separately timed stages.
Celebration is recorded without a consequent request to preserve the final image or event account.
The final defense instructions cannot establish a preservation-to-continuation pathway.
Insufficient room ends this expansion proposal through retention of the existing logo, making a loss-and-relocation pathway unnecessary for this episode.
Coordinates function as provisional instructions while design remains open rather than proving that a posted template settled it.
The explicit Tim call receives a bare assent, supporting this local pair without testing obligations of silent readers.
Distinguish an incoming offer of maintenance for building help from the host seeking aid because upkeep exhausted its hands.
Reciprocal-help bargaining opens the recorded exchange, so a prior border agreement cannot be inferred as its cause.
In the observed expansion episode a call for a larger mark ends in defending the small logo rather than proceeding with the anticipated fight.
An apology for looking threatening and reported preventive resizing do not establish an actual attack that caused restraint.
The incoming request for building help does not establish an attack that provoked negotiation.
The retreat-to-defense passage cannot establish an actual attack followed by a continuing spoken contest.
A maintenance proposal does not establish a coalition formed in response to a shared threat.
A call and difficulty finding updates across comments do not establish a flood of canvas posts producing containment.
A provisional request and possible agreement elsewhere cannot test whether an adopted local agreement would provoke a binding-authority dispute.
Willingness to assist a neighboring build is qualified by available space and whether maintained neighbors can be outnumbered.
A provisional agreement elsewhere can suspend a local request before the recorded location discussion reaches an outcome.
Keep missed updates across comments visible as a coordination difficulty within thread-based instructions.
A participant explicitly abandons expansion because suitable space is unavailable and chooses defending the existing smaller work.
A declaration of successful completion immediately becomes a call to build another target and receives assent.
